observations.observation: The page titles differ. The original is titled 'Thync | Neurostimulation For Everyone – Thync Global, Inc.' and the AI-built page is titled 'Thync – Wearable Neurostimulation'.

tags.value: changed: long brand title becomes short title and minimal meta

observations.observation: The landmark structure differs. The original has a header, 2 navs, a main and a footer, with 0 section, 0 article and 0 figure elements. The AI-built page has a header, 1 nav, a main and a footer, plus 6 sections, 3 articles, 8 figure/figcaption pairs, and native details/summary and form elements. Both pages have one main and one footer.

tags.value: changed: divs and figures become sections and articles

observations.observation: Markup weight and styling differ. The original is div-heavy (150 divs) and uses theme-specific classes (210 unique across 494 uses, 7.3% Tailwind-like) with 4 stylesheets and 20 inline style attributes. The AI-built page has 33 divs and hand-written CSS in one inline style block, with no external stylesheet. It uses 24 unique classes across 42 uses (2.4% Tailwind-like) and 6 inline style attributes.

tags.value: changed: heavy div markup becomes minimal markup

observations.observation: The heading outline differs. On the original, a hidden h2 'Just added to your cart' and an empty h3 come before an empty 18px/400 h1. The visible title 'Neurostimulation For Everyone' and the Q&A headings are h2s, and 'Our Approach To Science' is an h4. The AI-built page runs h1 ('Electricity is the brain's natural language.', 60.8px/700), then 6 section h2s, then h3s for the cards. Its footer column labels are also h3s.

tags.value: changed: flat empty h1 and many h2s becomes structured h1 h2 h3

observations.observation: The typeface differs. The original uses the Poppins web font on 346 elements, set light or regular. The AI-built page uses the system-ui stack on 169 elements, with no web fonts or stylesheet files, and sets its headings heavy and tightly tracked.

tags.value: changed: poppins web font becomes system-ui stack

observations.observation: Body text differs. The original sets dark gray rgb(58,58,58) text at 15px/22.5px on white, in columns about 540px wide. The AI-built page sets navy-black rgb(16,24,40) text at 17px/28.05px on off-white rgb(247,249,252), in blocks 640–680px wide.

tags.attribute: body text size and line height
tags.value: changed: 15px 1.5 becomes 17px 1.65
changed: white becomes off-white

observations.observation: The hero headline differs. The original's is about 50px, light-weight white Poppins with a text shadow, centered over a photo, with a subtitle below it. The AI-built page's is a 60.8px, weight-700 navy h1, left-aligned on two lines.

tags.value: changed: light white centered h1 becomes bold navy left-aligned h1

observations.observation: The hero background differs. The original uses a full-bleed 1440x810 photo of an athlete wearing the device, darkened by an rgba(0,0,0,0.4) overlay. The AI-built page has no hero image. Its hero sits on a soft gradient with a lavender wash at the top right and a mint-teal wash at the bottom left (4 gradient backgrounds on the page).

tags.value: changed: full-bleed photo becomes two-column gradient hero

observations.observation: Section title styling differs. The original's section titles are bold, widely letter-spaced and centered, and they contrast with lighter, left-aligned, roughly 24px Q&A headings. The AI-built page's section h2s are 35.2px, bold and left-aligned on a shared left edge.

tags.value: changed: centered letterspaced headings become left-aligned bold h2s

observations.observation: Small uppercase, letter-spaced teal eyebrow labels (for example 'NEWEST PRODUCT', 'ABOUT THYNC', 'PRESS COVERAGE') sit above the section headings.

tags.value: added: uppercase letterspaced eyebrow above headings

observations.observation: Both pages use a restrained palette with a single accent, but the accent and neutrals differ. The original uses orange rgb(241,126,74) with white and light-gray (#f7f7f7/#f6f6f6) surfaces and charcoal text. The AI-built page uses teal rgb(11,156,133) with navy-black text, slate-gray secondary text rgb(86,97,118), white cards and pale blue-gray bands.

tags.value: changed: orange accent becomes teal with navy text
changed: brand orange accent becomes teal

observations.observation: Sections alternate between off-white rgb(247,249,252) and pale blue-gray rgb(238,242,249) bands, so sections are separated by flat color rather than dividers.

tags.value: added: alternating off-white and pale blue bands

observations.observation: The header differs. The original has a white bar with a raster logo image on the left, centered nav links, 'FeelZing' styled as an orange filled button, and a thin shadow. The AI-built page has a slim, translucent off-white bar with backdrop blur, a text wordmark 'THYNC.' with a teal period, and four plain, small slate-gray links on the right with no button treatment.

tags.value: changed: separate inset bar becomes translucent blurred header nav
changed: raster logo becomes text wordmark

observations.observation: The primary CTA differs. The original has an orange 'DISCOVER FEELZING' button in uppercase with small tracking and square corners, and its secondary 'READ MORE' buttons are outlined in orange. The AI-built page has a solid teal pill (radius 999px) with white bold Title Case text, 'Discover Feelzing', which appears twice (hero and product section).

tags.value: changed: orange uppercase square button becomes teal pill button

observations.observation: Both pages have an inline 'feelzing.com' link within body copy, underlined. On the original it is in Q&A item 5; on the AI-built page it is colored teal.

tags.value: kept: underlined inline feelzing link

observations.observation: The five-question FAQ differs. The original uses numbered h2 questions in a zigzag two-column layout that alternates text and image on a roughly 1150px container. The AI-built page uses native details/summary accordions as white rounded bordered cards with a teal +/– indicator; the first is open and the other four are closed.

tags.value: changed: zigzag numbered q&a becomes details accordion cards

observations.observation: Several content images fail to render (natural size 0): the brain image and the Nature and bioRxiv thumbnails show alt text, and other slots appear as flat #f2f2f2 gray placeholders. This leaves empty areas beside the Q&A text.

tags.value: dropped: broken images and gray placeholders

observations.observation: The FAQ answers of the collapsed accordion items are empty in the DOM, and the last answer holds only an anchor with no text.

tags.value: added: empty collapsed answers in dom

observations.observation: Alt text coverage differs. The original has 2 images with no alt, several with empty alt, and others with hyphenated slug alts. On the AI-built page, all 8 images have alt text (alt_missing 0).

tags.value: changed: missing alts become descriptive alts

observations.observation: Both pages render the video as a large empty panel with a centered circular play button and no poster image. The original's is a flat gray 1152x650 square-cornered box with an orange play icon. The AI-built page's is a 1040x585 rounded panel with a pale gradient fill, an 84px teal play button and a figcaption naming the lead scientist.

tags.value: changed: gray empty video box becomes rounded gradient panel with teal play button

observations.observation: Both pages show the scientific papers as three columns in a row, but the cards differ. The original's have an image, a short summary and an outlined orange square 'READ MORE' button. The AI-built page's are white image-less cards of 333px, each with an h3 title, a summary and a teal 'Read more →' text link.

tags.value: changed: image cards with outlined buttons become text-only cards with link

observations.observation: The press section differs. The original shows six grayscale 150x81 logos (PBS, TechCrunch, Digital Trends, Inc., CNN, WSJ) evenly spaced in one bare row. The AI-built page shows seven white rounded tiles, each with a 96x96 grayscale logo and a figcaption naming the outlet.

tags.value: changed: bare logo row becomes white logo tiles with captions

observations.observation: The WSJ press tile is misaligned: its logo sits 5px higher than the others and its caption wraps to two lines.

tags.value: added: misaligned tile with wrapped caption

observations.observation: The hero ends with a row of three stat blocks ('2010 Founded', '10+ years', '2,000+ sessions'). Each has a bold figure over a gray caption and a teal left rule.

tags.value: added: hero stat blocks with teal left rule

observations.observation: A two-column product section pairs copy with a CSS gradient ring 'FEELZING' badge with a glow instead of a product photo, and the wordmark overruns the ring. No product photography appears on the page (svgs 0; the only images are press logos and a trust badge).

tags.value: added: css gradient ring badge instead of photo

observations.observation: The newsletter differs. On the original, 'Stay Informed About Thync' is one of the footer columns and appears to hold an empty form. On the AI-built page it is a standalone bordered, rounded gradient card, with a pill email input ('you@example.com') next to a teal pill 'Sign up' button.

tags.value: changed: footer column form becomes standalone card with pill input

observations.observation: The footer differs. The original is a light-gray rgb(246,246,246) band with a centered 'Follow us' label, three black inline-SVG social icons, and four columns: nav links, company links, a privacy notice with email, and the newsletter. The AI-built page uses a four-column grid: a brand column (wordmark, tagline, email) and three link columns under small uppercase h3s (EXPLORE, FOLLOW, LEGAL), with the social links as text.

tags.value: changed: light gray centered footer becomes four-column footer with text socials

observations.observation: Both pages repeat the main nav destinations as links in the footer. On the AI-built page, the footer's EXPLORE list adds Careers and Patents.

tags.value: kept: main nav links repeated in footer

observations.observation: Both footers carry a TRUSTe badge and '© 2021 Thync Global, Inc.', in different arrangements. The original places the 100x27 badge at the bottom left and the copyright at the right in small type. The AI-built page puts the copyright and 'Powered by Shopify' (both as links) at the left and the badge, upscaled to 147x44, at the right, above a thin rule.

tags.value: changed: truste badge moves right and upscaled

observations.observation: Both pages show Shopify ties in different ways. The original carries Shopify wallet and checkout meta tags and a hidden 'Just added to your cart' notice. The AI-built page has only a visible 'Powered by Shopify' footer link.

tags.value: changed: shopify meta tags become powered by link

observations.observation: Corner rounding differs. On the original, radii are almost all 0 (340 elements), with 7 small radii, 2 at 16px or more and no pills, so buttons are square. The AI-built page rounds its containers heavily (12 at 8–15px, 5 at 16px or more) and uses 6 pills for buttons, inputs and the badge.

tags.value: changed: square corners become small rounding and pills

observations.observation: Visual effects differ. The original has 0 gradients, 0 backdrop blur, 2 box shadows, 10 transitions, 2 animations and 1 transform. The AI-built page has 4 gradients, 1 backdrop blur, 1 box shadow (the badge glow), 3 transitions, 0 animations and 0 transforms, and defines its cards with thin borders.

tags.value: changed: few effects become gradients backdrop blur and many transitions

observations.observation: The page grid differs. The original is a 4675px-tall scroll using flex (27 elements, 0 grid) on a container about 1150px wide (x 144–1296). The AI-built page is 4294px tall on a single centered 1040px column (x 200–1240), using 18 grid and 13 flex elements. Both pages are 1440px wide.

tags.value: changed: flexbox-only becomes flex plus grid columns
changed: wide column becomes narrower centered column

observations.observation: Both pages use generous vertical whitespace. The original has gaps of about 150–300px between Q&A blocks. On the AI-built page, sections have about 70px of top padding and are tall relative to their content.

tags.value: kept: generous vertical whitespace

observations.observation: Copy voice differs. The original is a first-person-plural FAQ ('We build devices...') with numbered questions, 386 words, 1 em dash and 1 emoji. The AI-built page is short and declarative, with concrete figures and a mission statement, 309 words, 0 em dashes and 0 emoji. Neither page uses exclamation marks.

tags.value: changed: numbered first-person faq becomes short declarative copy

observations.observation: Head metadata and scripting differ. The original has description, Open Graph, Twitter card and theme-color tags, 2 JSON-LD blocks, 54 scripts and 12 noscript elements. The AI-built page has only charset, viewport and description metas, 0 JSON-LD blocks and 1 script.

tags.value: changed: rich social and json-ld meta becomes minimal meta

observations.observation: Interactive and ARIA counts differ. The original has 55 ARIA attributes, 10 buttons and 15 inline SVG icons. The AI-built page has 3 ARIA attributes, 2 buttons and 0 SVGs; its play glyph is the text character '▶'.

tags.value: changed: inline svg icons become text glyphs
